newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU prepared to compromise on chips for ITA deal.
newsitem.headline: EU prepared to compromise on chips for ITA deal.

text.p: The European Union is considering softening its opposition to a U.S.-Japan semiconductor alliance in order to allow progress on an International Technology Agreement, EU sources said on Tuesday.

They said the European Commission -- which negotiates EU trade policy -- was backing down from an ultimatum that insists on EU participation in the chip alliance before progress can be made on the ITA.

Sources said EU Trade Commissioner Sir Leon Brittan wrote on Tuesday to his U.S. counterpart Charlene Barshefsky to reiterate his opposition to the alliance, but the delicately-phrased letter aims to give her room to negotiate with U.S. producers for less damaging consequences for the European industry.
Washington and Tokyo signed an agreement in July which gives their respective semiconductor industries responsibilty for monitoring foreign access to their markets.
Brittan's letter is believed to accuse the U.S. and Japanese industries of "holding semiconductor trade hostage", but avoid direct criticism of governments.
